decision_question: 普通 source-tag purge 是否足够清除 benign 撤权后的跨层残留影响？
evidence_boundary: Deterministic simulation of a 4-layer memory mechanism; NOT an LLM run and NOT real user data. The residual-influence matrix shows, per derived layer, how much influence a source-tag base purge leaves behind. It proves the residue is mechanistically real, per-layer localizable, and cleared by cross-layer repair; it does NOT quantify prevalence in any deployed system or across real LLM memory stacks.
reading: CONTINUE-signal: with derived layers present, source-tag purge leaves 100% residual influence; cross-layer repair clears it (0%). Residue is localized to derived layers [summary=100%, cache=100%] while a base-only store purges cleanly. Benign revocation residue is real and purge-insufficiency is layer-attributable — supports continuing C03 as a benchmark+systems contribution.
title: Cross-layer revocation canary
